newsitem.title: USA: U.S. deplores army massacre in Burundi.
newsitem.headline: U.S. deplores army massacre in Burundi.

text.p: The United States Tuesday deplored the massacre of at least 122 refugees by Burundian troops and renewed its call for a ceasefire and all-party talks in the ethnically divided Central African state.

The victims, all Burundians, were expelled from Tanzania last Friday, accused of taking part in violence in their camps, and were killed the same day. A spokesman for Burundi's Tutsi-dominated army said troops shot the refugees when they tried to escape from a detention centre.
"The United States deplores the recent violence in Burundi," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns. "This massacre is only part of a pattern of violence that must cease."
"The United States continues to call for a ceasefire and all-party talks to restore stability to Burundi," Burns added.
Burundi's army is at war with Hutu rebels fighting for a greater political stake in the country. The military seized power last July, toppling the previous coalition government.
U.S. special envoy Howard Wolpe toured Burundi, Tanzania and Kenya last weekend, trying to promote a ceasefire.
